blocks.text: Q3 2026 review inquiry responses
HANGS Construction Services LLC
Quarter: quarter ended September 30, 2026
Asked by: the review team, October 23, 2026
Answered by: Dana Whitfield, Controller
Answered on: October 26, 2026
Status: answers in writing; not a representation letter
Q1 Revenue. Why is contract revenue higher than last quarter and than the budget?

Answer: Pier 9 Tech Center was at full framing crews all quarter and Alder Point moved into interior work. Rainier Commons and Weller Street started in the quarter. Revenue is the job schedule: costs to date against estimated total costs on every job. Subcontractor costs rose with the work, so payables and the retainage we hold back from subcontractors rose too.
Q2 Billings. Why did the job schedule move from billings ahead of revenue at June 30 to revenue ahead of billings at September 30?

Answer: Mostly Alder Point. Its estimate now includes pending change order PCO-14 for the MRI suite shielding redesign, $640,000, which we priced and submitted on August 28. The owner’s architect has reviewed the pricing and we expect the owner to sign it in November. We cannot bill it until it is signed.
Q3 Margins. Why is the gross margin lower than last quarter and the budget?

Answer: Tideflats Cold Storage. In August we found cracks in tilt-up wall panels and 14 panels are being recast, and our insulated metal panel supplier raised its price 9%. We revised the estimate at September 30 from $16,284,000 to $17,480,000. We have a backcharge claim against the panel precaster that we have not recorded. The job is still profitable. No other job’s estimate changed by more than a rounding amount.
Q4 Accrued wages. Why did accrued wages nearly double since June 30?
Answer: The September 30 accrual covers wages earned September 14 to 30, paid on October 2 and October 16. At June 30 the accrual covered only June 22 to 30.
Q5 Interest. How is interest on the Cinderbrook loans recorded?
Answer: Interest on both Cinderbrook loans is accrued monthly. The bank debits it on the first of the following month.
Q6 Cash and the line. Why is cash lower and the line of credit higher than at June 30?

Answer: We drew $1,200,000 on the line on August 14 to pay subcontractors on Pier 9 Tech Center while two owner payments were late. Receivables are up because September billings were larger and Juniper Ridge Holdings’ September billing was still open at quarter end.
Q7 Related parties. Do you have any transactions with related parties?

Answer: The Juniper Ridge Holdings job (J-2625), nine flex units, is built for Juniper Ridge Holdings LLC, a commercial developer with the same owners as HGC, building flex industrial buildings on land it owns. It is billed on the same terms as other owners.
Q8 Accounting changes. Did any accounting policy or estimate method change in the quarter?
Answer: No. We use the same cost-to-cost method and the same change order policy as at June 30.
Q9 Subsequent events. Has anything happened since September 30 that could affect the statements?
Answer: On October 9 we drew another $500,000 on the line. Lakeside Clinic started in October and was first billed on October 30.
Q10 Claims and litigation. Are there any claims, disputes or lawsuits by or against the company?
Answer: Only our backcharge claim against the Tideflats panel precaster. No owner has made a claim against us.
Q11 Covenants. Was the company in compliance with the Cinderbrook covenants at September 30?
Answer: Yes. Our compliance certificate goes to the bank by November 14, 2026.
Q12 Fraud and going concern. Do you know of any fraud or suspected fraud, or any doubt about the company continuing as a going concern?
Answer: No to both.
Demonstration document. Every name and figure is invented.

trail.what: Reading Q3 2026 comparative trial balance.xlsx
trail.result: Read Q3 2026 comparative trial balance.xlsx: 27 balance sheet and 15 income accounts, three columns each; “Q3 2026 close complete”.

trail.what: Reading Q3 2026 interim financial statements.pdf
trail.result: Read Q3 2026 interim financial statements.pdf: prepared by Dana Whitfield on October 21, 2026, 28 lines, not reviewed.

trail.what: Reading FY2027 operating budget.xlsx
trail.result: Read FY2027 operating budget.xlsx: 15 accounts by quarter. Approved by the board on June 18, 2026.

trail.what: Agree the trial balance’s three columns and tie the interim statements to it
trail.result: The trial balance balances in all three columns: September 30 with the quarter’s income accounts, June 30 after closing, and September 30, 2025 with that quarter. All 28 lines of Dana Whitfield’s interim statements agree with it at both dates, total assets $23,636,094.70. They are management’s own, “unaudited, not reviewed”, and have three short notes.

trail.what: Propose materiality from the quarter’s revenue, as the review plan sets it
trail.result: Contract revenue $21,696,700.00 x 0.5% = $108,483.50, rounded down to $100,000.00. Performance materiality $75,000.00; clearly trivial $5,000.00. A fluctuation is investigated when it is more than $50,000.00 and more than 10%. The engagement shareholder sets the final amounts.

trail.what: Plan the Review
trail.result: The trial balance and the statements agree · revenue $21,696,700 · materiality $100,000.00 proposed · investigate over $50,000 and 10%

trail.what: Compare the quarter’s income with the prior quarter, the same quarter last year and the budget
trail.result: Revenue $21,696,700.00 is $2,536,300.00 (13.2%) above the prior quarter and 37.0% above last year, but only 3.8% over budget. Gross margin fell to 8.28% from 10.20% last quarter and 10.50% budgeted, and net income $205,803.93 is $366,696.07 short of budget. Over the threshold: contract revenue, cost of revenue, gross profit, net income, and the margin.

trail.what: Compare the balance sheet with June 30 and with a year earlier
trail.result: 9 balance sheet lines moved more than the threshold since June 30. Billings ran $914,250.00 ahead of revenue at June 30 and $49,950.00 behind it at September 30, a $964,200.00 swing. Accrued wages rose from $314,193.69 to $598,629.52 (91%). Cash fell $1,399,296.01 while the line of credit rose $1,200,000.00 and receivables $2,142,125.00.

trail.what: Set an independent expectation for each figure the review can rebuild from other records
trail.result: Expectations set: revenue rebuilt job by job from the contract schedule; gross profit at each job’s June 30 margin; wages and accrued wages from the Q3 payroll ledger; interest from each loan’s balance, rate and days; retainage at 5% of billings. Every other flagged line is put to the controller in writing and corroborated where a record allows.

trail.what: Compare the Quarter
trail.result: Revenue up 13.2% · margin down to 8.28% · 14 fluctuations to explain

trail.what: Reading Q3 2026 review inquiry responses.docx
trail.result: Read Q3 2026 review inquiry responses.docx: 12 written answers from Dana Whitfield, October 26, 2026.

trail.what: Record the controller’s written answer to each flagged fluctuation
trail.result: Dana Whitfield answered all 12 questions in writing on October 26, 2026. Every one of the 14 flagged lines and the margin has an answer: revenue and costs (Q1), the billing swing (Q2: pending change order PCO-14 on Alder Point), the margin (Q3: Tideflats estimate revised), accrued wages (Q4), cash and the line (Q6). Q5 says interest is accrued monthly. Each answer is corroborated against a record before it is relied on.

trail.what: Look for related parties and for what the statements say about them
trail.result: Q7: the Juniper Ridge Holdings job (J-2625), nine flex units, is built for Juniper Ridge Holdings LLC, a commercial developer under the same owners, building flex industrial buildings on land it owns. The trial balance carries $571,000.00 due from it on account 1210, which the statements fold into contract receivables. The statements have no related party note (RP-01). Other answers: no accounting changes (Q8); a further $500,000.00 drawn on the line on October 9 (Q9); no claims against HGC (Q10); covenants said to be met (Q11, tested in stage 5); no fraud or going concern doubt known (Q12).

trail.what: Ask Management
trail.result: 12 written answers recorded · related party: Juniper Ridge Holdings LLC (J-2625) · Q5 interest answer to test

trail.what: Reading September 30 2026 contract schedule.xlsx
trail.result: Read September 30 2026 contract schedule.xlsx: 7 jobs at September 30 and 6 at June 30.

trail.what: Recompute earned revenue on every job and tie the quarter’s revenue and costs to the books
trail.result: Every job’s earned revenue recomputes: cost to date over estimated total cost, times the total contract. Earned to date rose from $22,308,250.00 to $44,004,950.00: $21,696,700.00, the quarter’s contract revenue in the books to the cent. Costs to date rose $19,899,372.50, the cost of revenue in the books. Pier 9 Tech Center and Alder Point account for $13,698,950.00 of it, and two jobs started in the quarter, as Q1 says.

trail.what: Explain the billing swing and recompute the retainage
trail.result: The schedule’s underbillings $390,950.00 and overbillings $341,000.00 are the books’ at both dates. The quarter billed $20,732,500.00 against $21,696,700.00 of revenue: the $964,200.00 difference is the swing exactly. Alder Point alone moved $612,950.00, from $337,500.00 overbilled to $275,450.00 underbilled, as Q2 says. Retainage receivable $2,197,750.00 is 5% of $43,955,000.00 billed to date.

trail.what: Test each job’s margin for the quarter against its June 30 estimate
trail.result: At June 30 margins the quarter’s jobs would have earned $2,180,047.50 of gross profit; they earned $1,797,327.50. One job explains it: Tideflats Cold Storage earned $82,800.00 on $4,048,000.00 of revenue, $382,720.00 below its June margin, because its estimate rose from $16,284,000.00 to $17,480,000.00 and the whole year-to-date effect lands in this quarter. That is the revision Q3 describes. The job still expects a 5.0% margin, so no loss provision is needed; the backcharge claim is rightly not recorded (JOB-01).

trail.what: Test the change order the schedule counts before the owner has signed it
trail.result: Alder Point’s total contract includes pending change order PCO-14, $640,000.00, which the owner has not signed (Q2). At 40.5% complete it puts $259,200.00 into this quarter’s revenue and gross profit, more than materiality. Whether an unsigned change order can be counted yet is a judgment under the revenue standard’s limit on uncertain amounts; the CPA reads the pricing and the architect’s review (REV-01). Without it Alder Point would be $16,250.00 against its billings.

trail.what: Corroborate the Jobs
trail.result: Revenue and costs tie to the jobs · the $964,200 swing explained · Tideflats $382,720 below its June margin · PCO-14 $259,200 unsigned

trail.result: Field wages $2,239,385.83, office salaries $726,137.98, employer Social Security and Medicare $193,087.43 and labor vendors $541,093.00 are the payroll ledger’s to the cent. Accrued wages are its two accrual journals: $314,193.69 at June 30 (June 22 to 30, paid July 10), reversed July 1, and $598,629.52 at September 30 (September 14 to 30). The increase is the calendar, as Q4 says: about 13 working days accrued at September 30 against 7 at June 30. No adjustment.

passages.q: Must HANGS Construction Services file Form 940 for 2026?
passages.a: You're subject to FUTA tax in 2026 on the wages you pay employees who aren't farmworkers or household workers if: you paid wages of $1,500 or more in any calendar quarter in 2025 or 2026, or you had one or more employees for at least some part of a day in any 20 or more different weeks in 2025 or 20 or more different weeks in 2026.

passages.q: What are the 2026 FUTA rate, wage base and credit?
passages.a: For 2026, the FUTA tax rate is 6.0%. The tax applies to the first $7,000 you pay to each employee as wages during the year. ... The credit may be as much as 5.4% of FUTA taxable wages. If you're entitled to the maximum 5.4% credit, the FUTA tax rate after credit is 0.6%.

passages.q: Do employees' 401(k) deferrals come off FUTA wages?
passages.a: Elective employee contributions and deferrals to a plan containing a qualified cash or deferred compensation arrangement (401(k)). Generally exempt, but see section 402(g) for limitation. Taxable. Taxable.

passages.q: When is the Q3 2026 Form 941 due?
passages.a: Your Form 941 is due by the last day of the month that follows the end of the quarter. ... 3. July, August, September September 30 October 31 ... If you made timely deposits in full payment of your taxes for the quarter, you may file by the 10th day of the 2nd month that follows the end of the quarter. ... If any due date for filing falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, you may file your return on the next business day.

passages.q: Which employees are counted on line 1, and what goes on lines 2 and 3?
passages.a: Enter the number of employees on your payroll for the pay period including March 12, June 12, September 12, or December 12, for the quarter indicated at the top of Form 941. ... Enter amounts on line 2 that would also be included in box 1 of your employees’ Forms W-2. ... Enter the federal income tax you withheld (or were required to withhold) from your employees on this quarter’s wages, tips, taxable fringe benefits, and supplemental unemployment compensation benefits.

passages.q: Which wages go on line 5a, and where does Social Security stop for each employee?
passages.a: The social security tax rate is 6.2% each for the employee and employer. The social security wage base limit is $184,500. ... For 2026, the rate of social security tax on taxable wages is 6.2% (0.062) each for the employer and employee. Stop paying social security tax on and entering an employee’s wages on line 5a when the employee’s taxable wages and tips reach $184,500 for the year. ... line 5a (column 1) x 0.124 line 5a (column 2)

sources.title: General Instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3 (2026)

passages.q: When are the 2026 Forms W-2 and W-3 due, and must they be e-filed?
passages.a: The due date for filing 2026 Forms W-2 ... and W-3 ... with the SSA is February 1, 2027, whether you file using paper forms or electronically. ... Generally, you must furnish Copies B, C, and 2 of Form W-2 to your employees by February 1, 2027. ... You must e-file Forms W-2 ... if you are required to file at least 10 information returns.

passages.q: What goes in box 1, and are the 401(k) deferrals and Washington Paid Leave premiums in it?
passages.a: Box 1-Wages, tips, other compensation. Show the total taxable wages, tips, and other compensation that you paid to your employee during the year. However, do not include elective deferrals (such as employee contributions to a section 401(k) or 403(b) plan) ... You must include the employee contribution and the employer voluntary payment as wages on the Form W-2.

passages.q: What are the 2026 Social Security limits for boxes 3 and 4, and what goes in boxes 5 and 6?
passages.a: The total of boxes 3 and 7 cannot exceed $184,500 (2026 maximum social security wage base). ... For 2026, the amount should not exceed $11,439 ... there is no wage base limit for Medicare tax ... an employer is required to withhold a 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax on any Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA) wages ... in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year.

checks.title: REV-01
checks.detail: Alder Point’s schedule counts pending change order PCO-14, $640,000.00 for the MRI suite shielding redesign, submitted August 28 and not signed by the owner. It adds $259,200.00 to the quarter’s revenue and gross profit, 259% of materiality. Revenue from an unapproved change order may be counted only when it is probable that a significant reversal will not occur. The CPA reads the change order, the owner’s and architect’s correspondence and the history of approvals on this owner, and decides. The machine counts nothing either way.

checks.title: INT-01
checks.detail: Interest is recorded when Cinderbrook Bank debits it, not as it accrues. September’s interest, $35,350.00 on the bank’s statement, is not in the books, and June’s $28,665.00 was recorded in July. Expense for the quarter is understated $6,685.00, 6.7% of materiality, and accrued interest by $35,350.00. Proposed: debit interest expense $6,685.00 and shareholders’ equity $28,665.00 (June’s interest, a correction of FY2026, if the CPA treats it so), credit 2410 accrued interest $35,350.00. Under performance materiality: passed if the client declines. The machine never posts.

checks.title: COV-01
checks.detail: Tangible net worth as the loan agreement defines it is $6,629,999.00, $129,999.00 above the $6,500,000 minimum, after leaving out $715,500.00 due from Juniper Ridge Holdings, an affiliate. With INT-01 recorded and PCO-14 left out it would be $6,335,449.00, short by $164,551.00: an event of default unless the bank waives it, which could make the line of credit and the term loan current. Working capital $4,789,499.00 and leverage 2.46 to 1 stay within their limits either way. The controller says the certificate goes to the bank by November 14 (Q11). The CPA decides REV-01 first, then the covenant and the debt classification.

checks.title: RP-01
checks.detail: The Juniper Ridge Holdings job (J-2625), nine flex units, is built for Juniper Ridge Holdings LLC, a commercial developer under the same owners, building flex industrial buildings on land it owns (Q7). It earned $1,638,000.00 of revenue in the quarter, and $715,500.00 is due from it in receivables, retainage and underbillings. The interim statements fold it into contract receivables and have no related party note. The CPA decides the disclosure; the bonding company and the lender read these statements.

checks.title: JOB-01
checks.detail: Tideflats Cold Storage’s estimate rose from $16,284,000.00 to $17,480,000.00 (14 tilt-up panels recast, a 9% panel price increase; Q3). The cumulative effect, $382,720.00 below the June margin, is in this quarter, which is how a change in estimate is recorded. The job still expects a profit, so no loss provision. The backcharge against the precaster is not recorded, which is right while it is only a claim. The CPA reads the revised estimate and the recast quotes.

checks.title: INQ-01
checks.detail: The controller answered in writing that interest on both loans is accrued monthly (Q5). The bank’s statement and the books show it is not. Every other answer was corroborated by a record. The CPA considers what this means for relying on the answers and asks how the controller closes the quarter.

checks.title: SUB-01
checks.detail: After the quarter, HGC drew a further $500,000.00 on the line of credit on October 9 and started Lakeside Clinic (Q9). Neither changes the September 30 figures; the CPA decides whether the statements should mention the borrowing.

checks.title: MAT-01
checks.detail: Materiality is proposed at $100,000.00, 0.5% of the quarter’s revenue, with performance materiality $75,000.00, clearly trivial $5,000.00 and a $50,000.00 threshold for investigating a change. The engagement shareholder sets the final amounts.

checks.title: REP-01
checks.detail: No management representation letter has been obtained. A review needs one, dated near the date of the CPA’s report, covering the answers relied on here.

checks.title: SIGN-01
checks.detail: These are draft workpapers and a draft review memo for the engagement shareholder. They are not a review report and express no conclusion. Nothing has been signed, posted or sent to the client, the bank or the bonding company.

All 28 lines of Dana Whitfield’s interim statements agree with it at both dates, total assets $23,636,094.70. They are management’s own, “unaudited, not reviewed”, and have three short notes.

checks.title: Propose materiality from the quarter’s revenue, as the review plan sets it
checks.detail: Contract revenue $21,696,700.00 x 0.5% = $108,483.50, rounded down to $100,000.00. Performance materiality $75,000.00; clearly trivial $5,000.00. A fluctuation is investigated when it is more than $50,000.00 and more than 10%. The engagement shareholder sets the final amounts.

checks.title: Compare the quarter’s income with the prior quarter, the same quarter last year and the budget
checks.detail: Revenue $21,696,700.00 is $2,536,300.00 (13.2%) above the prior quarter and 37.0% above last year, but only 3.8% over budget. Gross margin fell to 8.28% from 10.20% last quarter and 10.50% budgeted, and net income $205,803.93 is $366,696.07 short of budget. Over the threshold: contract revenue, cost of revenue, gross profit, net income, and the margin.

checks.title: Compare the balance sheet with June 30 and with a year earlier
checks.detail: 9 balance sheet lines moved more than the threshold since June 30. Billings ran $914,250.00 ahead of revenue at June 30 and $49,950.00 behind it at September 30, a $964,200.00 swing. Accrued wages rose from $314,193.69 to $598,629.52 (91%). Cash fell $1,399,296.01 while the line of credit rose $1,200,000.00 and receivables $2,142,125.00.

checks.title: Set an independent expectation for each figure the review can rebuild from other records

Every other flagged line is put to the controller in writing and corroborated where a record allows.

checks.title: Record the controller’s written answer to each flagged fluctuation
checks.detail: Dana Whitfield answered all 12 questions in writing on October 26, 2026. Every one of the 14 flagged lines and the margin has an answer: revenue and costs (Q1), the billing swing (Q2: pending change order PCO-14 on Alder Point), the margin (Q3: Tideflats estimate revised), accrued wages (Q4), cash and the line (Q6). Alder Point alone moved $612,950.00, from $337,500.00 overbilled to $275,450.00 underbilled, as Q2 says. Retainage receivable $2,197,750.00 is 5% of $43,955,000.00 billed to date.
